## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64d2062396a8ec8b5495d964337862a777411224`
Local-runs: none

**Inputs.** Card objectui#12035 (body; comments 6076908444 deferral, 6078418546 claim, 6079270263 `os-dev-report`), its parent objectui#11794 item 5 with triage 6076172515, PR #12048 (body, 17-file list, the net diff against `main`; merge-base `5275d1f`, and `origin/main` is one commit ahead at `3c3115e`, touching none of these 17 paths), and the check-runs on the head. Files at the head and at `main` were read with `git show`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head, as read at 2026-10-09T10:49:58Z.** 42 runs: 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard)`), 8 `in_progress`: `Test (shard 1/8)` through `Test (shard 8/8)`. An in-progress gate is not a pass; the eight shard verdicts are not in this record. `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Build & E2E`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Docs Route Eager Closure Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec Main Shape Gate` and `Pre-Install Import Graph Check` are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Entry accept set (who enters Studio): unchanged — RIGHT.** The diff to `RequireStudioAccess` touches one return: the non-holder branch, which drew a `Navigate` element to `redirectTo ?? homePath` and now draws the module-private `StudioAccessRequired` with `home={homeTo ?? homePath}`. `holdsStudioAccess`, the pending branch (`LoadingFallback`) and the failed branch (`LoadingScreen` with `onRetry`) are byte-identical to `main`. The builder stays unmounted for a non-holder (`Outlet` is never reached), so its lazy chunk is still never requested. The card's "no change to who has access" holds.
- **Public surface of `@object-ui/i18n`: one member added — RIGHT, and correctly declared.** `packages/i18n/package.json` exports `.`, `./locales` and `./locales/*`; `TranslationKeys` is `typeof en` and is exported from the entry. The new key `console.studio.accessRequired` sits in the `console.studio` block of all ten packs (`ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh`, one row each, same path, beside `title`); no key is removed or renamed; the nine non-en values are translations, not the en sentence. This is a purely additive widening of a published accept set, so `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right line, and it is spelled the same in the PR body, the claim comment and the changeset.
- **Public surface of `@object-ui/console`: none — RIGHT.** Its `exports` map is `.` to `plugin.js` only (`plugin.ts` exports `ConsolePlugin` and `staticPath`); `dist` is shipped bytes, not an addressable accept set. `RequireStudioAccess` and its prop are not reachable through the map, and `git grep` at the head finds no caller passing `redirectTo` or `homeTo`. The rename is internal.
- **The reused label `empty.appAccessDeniedHome`: RIGHT.** Present in all ten packs on `main`; this diff adds a second read site (the first is `AppContent`'s app refusal). Exactly one key is added, as the card's ruling asks. Both inline `defaultValue` strings equal the en pack values, which is the premise `check:i18n-keys` reads.
- **Imports and dependencies: RIGHT.** New to the module: `Link`, `Lock`, `Button`, `Empty`, `EmptyTitle`; `useObjectTranslation` and `useHomePath` were already imported on `main`; `Navigate` is still read by the `:packageId` and org-scope redirect routes. `lucide-react`, `@object-ui/components`, `react-router-dom` and `@testing-library/user-event` are declared in `apps/console` `devDependencies` and already imported by 28, 31 and 32 other console sources respectively. `Lint` and `Type Check` are `success` on the head.
- **DOM contract of the new screen: RIGHT.** `Empty` spreads its props, so `data-testid="studio-access-required"` reaches the element; `Button asChild` renders through `Slot`, so the way home is a real router `Link` with an `href` the tests can read. The shape copies `AppContent`'s `empty.appAccessDenied` screen (in place, URL kept, no Retry).
- **Tests: RIGHT.** `StudioRoute.test.tsx` moves each refusal pin from "landed on `/home`" to "sentence on screen, URL unmoved, link to the home the redirect used", and the objectui#7373 pins click the link and land there; the holder, pending, failed and unauthenticated cases now also assert the notice is absent. The new `StudioRoute.accessNotice-12035.test.tsx` installs each of the ten packs and expects that pack's value, read from the pack. `lazyBuilder-11798` and `recentPackage-11863` only swap their decided-state signal; what they pin (no builder module load, no recent record) is unchanged.
- **Prose faces.** The changeset body and the `content/docs/guide/console.md` row are the dispatching seat's ACCEPT read, not this record's; noted only that both describe the code as it is at the head.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — RIGHT** (see ① above).
- **`.changeset/12035-studio-access-notice.md` grades `@object-ui/i18n: patch` and `@object-ui/console: patch` — WRONG on `@object-ui/i18n`.** The widening this PR declares lives in `@object-ui/i18n` and nowhere else: the changeset's own last paragraph says so ("the exported `en` pack and the `TranslationKeys` type derived from it gain one member"). The written rule is that a `Clause-②: yes` declaration takes at least `minor` (objectstack `AGENTS.md`, Post-Task Checklist item 3: "`yes` takes at least **`minor`**"; the fleet's `Check Changeset` level axis, #16055 and #16361: "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface takes AT LEAST `minor`", read at the PR's grain as "a PR that declares clause-② `yes` must grade AT LEAST ONE package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves at `minor` or above"). This PR grades no package at `minor`, so the declaration and the level contradict each other inside one PR. objectui's own `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` carries no level axis (it refuses `major` and nothing else), so the green `Changeset Bump Policy` run on this head carries no information on this axis; that is what this record is for.
- **The cited precedent does not carry this case.** `11863-studio-search.md` and `11863-studio-recent-packages.md` grade `@object-ui/i18n: patch` under `yes (widening)`, but in both the declared widening is `@object-ui/app-shell`'s (graded `minor`) and the pack rows ride beside it. Here the pack key is the sole widening and the sole reason the line reads `yes`. The on-point precedents pending on `main` — `11605-i18n-view-no-object.md`, `11666-launcher-plan-awaiting-approval.md`, `11720-org-slug-environments.md`, `11811-disabled-action-reason.md` — all grade `@object-ui/i18n: minor` under `yes (widening)`.
- **`@object-ui/console: patch` — RIGHT.** No published surface moves; a user-visible fix in a released package takes `patch`.
- **Remedy, one line:** grade `'@object-ui/i18n': minor` in `.changeset/12035-studio-access-notice.md`. Nothing else in the diff needs to move. The fixed group already has pending `minor` entries, so no version number changes; what changes is that the declaration becomes self-consistent and the entry publishes under the CHANGELOG heading it belongs to. Re-render this record on the next head.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's `os-dev-report` (6079270263) carries eight deviations, one `open_questions` entry and two out-of-scope findings. Each answered:

1. **`redirectTo` renamed `homeTo`.** Accepted. Not on the `exports` map, no caller at the head; the docblock explains why the old name no longer describes the prop.
2. **`content/docs/guide/console.md` gained one row.** Accepted. The claim lists the console guide "if it describes the `/studio` guard"; after this change the guard has user-visible behaviour, and AGENTS.md rule #2 asks the guide to say so. Prose face: the dispatching seat reads it at ACCEPT.
3. **Two sibling pin files edited** (`lazyBuilder-11798`, `recentPackage-11863`). Accepted: they are "the tests beside these" in the claim, and their load-bearing assertions are unchanged.
4. **A second worktree at the base, since removed.** Process only; nothing on the board. Noted.
5. **H3 measured with `vite build`, not the package build script.** Accepted; `Bundle Analysis` and `Docs Route Eager Closure Check` are `success` on the head.
6. **Browser evidence against a stand-in backend.** Accepted with the limit the dev states. The card's two pins (the sentence in the caller's locale; a holder enters as today) are carried by the ten-pack test and its holder control, with the browser leg as corroboration in en and zh.
7. **Model-free commit trailers.** Matches objectui `AGENTS.md`; both branch commits (`bf3ced6`, `64d2062`) carry the prescribed pair, the session link trailer and the co-author trailer, and nothing model-named.
8. **No labels written.** Fine; the four labels on the PR are the path labeler's.
- **`open_questions` — the way home reuses `empty.appAccessDeniedHome`. Answer: option A, keep the reuse.** The ruling fixes exactly one new key, for the sentence; the label is the console's existing "Back to home" of the refusal screen whose shape this copies, means the same on both, and is present in all ten packs. No rule in objectui `AGENTS.md` bars a second read site for a pack key. `MarketplaceAccessDenied`'s own `marketplace.action.backHome` is a namespace choice, not a prohibition. If the app screen's wording ever diverges, a dedicated key is a one-row widening with its own changeset. Not escalated.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `11798-console-eager-closure.md`'s "the Studio entry gate is unchanged" sentence.** Agreed: it describes that change's own effect, and the gate's decision is unchanged here; `Changeset Claim Re-read` is `success`. Not amended.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `RequireAiSurface` still redirects silently.** Agreed it is outside this card (an availability gate, not a permission refusal). Nothing filed by this record; the maintainer may card it separately.

**Why FAIL rather than PASS-with-note:** ② is a contradiction between the PR's own declaration and the level it grades the one package that carries it, on the axis this tier exists to read. ① and ③ hold as written, the fix is one word in one file, and the eight test shards were still in progress at the reading above.
